card.title: Fair Exchange
card.instruction: Price every favor in time, effort, inconvenience, or future obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Half an hour helping you move buys two hours painting my shed on Saturday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Saturday's my only lie-in. Can I come after lunch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Afternoon painting costs me cricket. Three hours, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hire a painter. But I need the sofa carried up three flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then two painter-hours covers loading; the stairs cost a third. Cricket's free again.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 moving time buys painting hours, A3 lost cricket adds cost and A5 stairs add hired labor while restoring cricket freedom.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 afternoon request causes A3 opportunity-cost increase; B4 painter substitute and stairs cause A5 task-based repricing.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects a lie-in and B4 offers an outside worker while clarifying the physical moving task.

heightening.evidence: B4 removes A's time sacrifice but increases lifting difficulty, so A5 separates the two costs accurately within the bargain.

specificity.evidence: A1 move and shed painting plus B2 Saturday establish the tradable work and time.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 cricket free again explicitly uses B4 hired-painter change rather than repeats the earlier rate.
